correctness.rationale: The Fourier block characteristic equation gives an injective relation between each eigenvalue and its Bloch root because λ=-s is excluded by rs>0. The discriminant conditions have exactly the positive solutions r=pη(1-η),s=pη(1+η) for η=sin(πk/n), k not zero or n/2. Fourier pairs k and n-k give two conjugate double defective eigenvalues with two size-2 Jordan blocks; all remaining modes are simple. The directly measured inactive Fourier component equals ru exp(λu) from the nilpotent block exponential. The shared parabola, density and maximal r bound follow algebraically. Independently assembled full 2n-state matrix exponentials confirmed 100 numerical cases, and 420 Jordan plus 900 off-locus checks passed; finite checks are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Non-Hermitian exceptional points are physically motivated by transient motor-network relaxation, and the exact classification gives all positive-rate design coordinates for every ring size rather than a sampled or contrived finite matrix. The sharp r≤p/4 constraint, divisibility-by-six equality condition, global rate parabola, dense union and exact polynomially enhanced Fourier probability pulse constitute a structural, potentially reusable mathematical benchmark. The result does not rely on unsupported experimental claims.
